data.bottom_line: With new glide cracks appearing and glide avalanches occurring daily, glide avalanches are the main concern in the Turnagain Pass and Girdwood zone. Avoid traveling underneath them when possible, and spread out if you can't avoid traveling underneath. Although we aren’t seeing anything too concerning in the snowpack layering, we still have limited information. If you are getting out on steep terrain, choose slopes with clean runouts to avoid a poor outcome if you get surprised. At lower elevations, some early season hazards still exist, including open water, bare ground, and alders just beneath the snow. __________________________________ SPECIAL ANNOUNCEMENTS: Forecast Operations: Daily danger ratings for Turnagain Pass begin Saturday, November 28. Weekly danger ratings for Chugach State Park and Summit Lake also begin on Saturday, November 28. On December 2nd and 3rd, the Northern Aspects Film Festival 2026 will be showing at Bear Tooth Theatrepub for its fifth year, celebrating the people, places, and stories that make skiing in Alaska unlike anywhere else. These showings will benefit the Hatcher Pass Avalanche Center and the Valdez Avalanche Center. Hope to see you there! Motorized Winter Access: Turnagain Pass opens to snowmachines on Wednesday, November 25, the day before Thanksgiving, per the CNF Forest plan and the new over-snow vehicle use map ( OSVU map ). The remaining motorized winter riding areas on the Chugach National Forest open December 1. Happy Thanksgiving from all of us at the Chugach National Forest Avalanche Center! We hope you enjoy the snowy holiday.
